attribution.note: These are Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, stated in his own voice. He is not quoting anyone.

semantics.note: The proposition matches the text and keeps the 'do not appear' qualifier. It joins a checkable claim about burn with a qualified, subjective judgement about whether either company had found a way to stop.

contract.note: The contract fairly declines a single verdict. Zitron set no threshold for 'appear to have found a way', and a management forecast alone does not refute a qualified impression. Reading 'billions' as at least $2B in 2024 is an ordinary reading of the financial part.

evidence.note: CNBC, Sept 2024: OpenAI expected about $5B of losses for 2024. This was a projection made mid-year, not a completed-year result, so under the contract it cannot settle the financial part for OpenAI.

A LinkedIn summary of The Information reports Anthropic burned $5.6B in 2024 and planned to cut that by nearly half. The figure is secondhand and comes from the company. It fits the financial part but does not settle the judgement.

Reuters syndication, Feb 12, 2025: Anthropic management expects to stop burning cash in 2027. Zitron acknowledged this forecast and expressed doubt about it, so it does not contradict his qualified impression.

reviews.rationale: I can't score this as one claim. The second half, that the companies do not appear to have found a way to stop, is a qualified judgement with no threshold, so not adjudicable. On the financial half, Anthropic's reported $5.6B burn for 2024 fits, but it is a company figure passed on by the press. OpenAI's $5B is a mid-2024 projection, which the contract says cannot stand in for a completed result. The packet does not settle the financial half on its own terms either.
